keyLimits.en: Lifetime license activatable on 2 computers (Mac and/or PC); upgrade pricing from versions 8/9 available from $84.99.
Lifetime license activatable on 3 computers; adds advanced features over Essential (e.g. more correction tools); upgrade from Essential costs $99.

cautions.en: No subscription option exists; both editions are perpetual, one-time-purchase licenses, with paid upgrade pricing for future major versions.
License requires periodic online reactivation; offline usage is limited to 37 days after the last online activation.

capabilities.en: End-to-end RAW photo editing with DxO's optics-based automatic corrections (lens sharpness, distortion, vignetting).
AI-powered denoising and other AI features, which require a dedicated GPU (NVIDIA RTX 3000+, AMD Radeon RX6000+, Intel ARC, or Apple M1+).
Available in English, French, German, Japanese and Simplified Chinese.

limitations.en: No monthly subscription plan; buyers pay a full one-time price per major version, with separate paid upgrades for future releases.
AI features require a fairly recent, capable GPU (8GB VRAM minimum on supported cards), which not all users' machines will have.
License activation is capped at 2 computers on Essential and 3 on Elite, with only 37 days of offline use before requiring reactivation.

reason.en: Dominant subscription-based RAW editor and asset manager, the main alternative for photographers comparing pricing models.
Professional RAW editing competitor offering both subscription and perpetual license options.
Free, open-source RAW editor alternative for users who don't want to pay for a perpetual license.

unknowns: Trial duration/availability for DxO PhotoLab 10 was not stated on the shop pages checked.
Precise feature differences between Essential and Elite editions beyond activation count were not fully itemized on the pages checked.
conflicts: The current product version is DxO PhotoLab 10 (Essential $159.99 / Elite $249.99), not version 7/8 or the $99.99 Essential price implied by the seed data's earlier pricingText, which appears outdated.
